summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with recurrent chest pain following a dialysis session and a recent history of subsegmental pulmonary embolism. Initial evaluation confirmed resolution of the pulmonary embolism on CT angiography and ruled out acute coronary syndrome. The chest pain was determined to be musculoskeletal, consistent with costochondritis, and improved with methocarbamol. The patient was subtherapeutic on warfarin, so she was bridged with unfractionated heparin until her INR reached a therapeutic level of 2.5. Her home medications were continued, with adjustments for safety and administration, including switching to crushed short-acting nitrates and changing phosphate binders to lanthanum due to her inability to swallow pills. Concerns about safety at her previous rehabilitation facility were addressed, and a transfer to a new extended care center was arranged. She was discharged in stable condition with a plan for ongoing anticoagulation, dialysis, and physical therapy.
